subject: Consolidated MAP: SOC 2 checkpoints, DPA redline & retention proposal — BrightBridge
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightbridge.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidated MAP kickoff — security checkpoints we need to close

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short MAP focused on the security/compliance items that will gate a production go-live for BrightBridge. To keep things actionable, we split items into three buckets: evidence (SOC 2), contract (DPA redline), and operational (retention & residency).

Can you confirm whether BrightBridge can:
- Share your latest SOC 2 attestation (PDF) and the date range it covers
- Accept a limited-data retention schedule (30 / 90 / 365 days buckets) or propose your preferred windows
- Indicate any specific SIG/CAIQ control gaps we should expect so we can scope remediation for the MAP

If you can attach the SOC 2 attestation and a quick note on retention preferences, our legal and security teams will route a DPA markup and a short evidence intake checklist. Target closing the MAP in three weeks (target sign by 2027-09-29) — reasonable?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the internal owners for each ask.

—Priyom
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: MAP_onepager_v0.3.pdf (summary)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@brightbridge.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-09T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated MAP kickoff — security checkpoints we need to close

Priyom —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. Attached our SOC 2 Type II attestation and an internal retention matrix that reflects our current posture. Quick notes:
- SOC 2 Type II (2026-08-01 to 2027-07-31) attached as BrightBridge_SOC2_Attestation_2027.pdf
- We generally support the 30/90/365 buckets for user-level logs, but financial transaction artifacts are on a 5-year ledger in our systems (we can scope how that maps to Redwood-hosted artifacts)
- On SIG/CAIQ: we have two expected gaps around encrypted backups (process doc in progress) and multi-region key rotation cadence — happy to share more detail in a follow-up.

I've looped in Nora (security ops) to help answer specific evidence intake questions. Please send your DPA markup and retention proposal and we’ll turn around comments.

Alex
CISO, BrightBridge
Attachments: BrightBridge_SOC2_Attestation_2027.pdf, Retention_Table_BrightBridge.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightbridge.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-12T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood DPA markups + clarification on retention/residency

Alex / Priyom —

Thanks for sending the SOC and retention matrix. I’m attaching a proposed DPA markup (Redwood_DPA_Markup_v1.docx) with three commercial/legal items to confirm:
1) Data categories: we’ve scoped "Redwood Logs" (inference request metadata and token traces) and "Customer Payloads" (customer-provided inputs). Please confirm whether BrightBridge considers ledger-level financial artifacts to be in-scope for the Redwood-hosted inference path or out-of-scope (we can carve out ledger replication if needed).
2) Retention windows: Redwood proposes default retention by data category: 30 days for Logs, 90 days for short-term artifacts, 365 days for model training opt-ins. If BrightBridge requires the 5-year ledger retention for any data that flows through Redwood, we need a documented business justification and a plan for escrow/archival; that will affect pricing and on-prem options.
3) International residency: BrightBridge listed US + EU in their intake. Confirm whether EU residency is required for inference outputs tied to EU customers — if yes, we’ll propose a Dedicated region pin.

Operational asks for MAP closure: evidence upload link (we’ll provide an intake form) and an acceptance call with Security + Legal w/c 2027-09-20. If we can get DPA redlines back by end-of-week (9/17), we can keep the target sign date of 9/29.

On the SIG/CAIQ gaps you mentioned: can Nora share the backup encryption schedule and an ETA for the process doc? Those two items map directly to our evidence sprint and will determine whether we need an interim compensating control.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Markup_v1.docx

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora.singh@brightbridge.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA markups + clarification on retention/residency

Kimberly / Team —

Thanks — Nora and I reviewed your markup. Short answers:
- Ledger data: BrightBridge agrees ledger-level financial artifacts are out-of-scope for Redwood inference (we will not route long-term ledger replication through Redwood). We’ll provide a short statement to that effect for the DPA.
- Retention: We can accept the proposed default windows for Logs (30), short-term artifacts (90), and model opt-ins (365). Nora attached a short spreadsheet with the agreed mapping.
- EU residency: We have a subset of EU transactions that must stay in EU. We accept Redwood’s Dedicated-region pin approach — Nora will confirm which account segments need it.

Next steps: Nora to upload the backup encryption process doc by EOD 2027-09-17. We will return a single redline to Redwood legal by 2027-09-17 confirming the limited carveout for ledger data. Assuming that, Alex and Priyom confirmed that target sign of 2027-09-29 is viable.

I’ll schedule an acceptance call for 2027-09-20 at 10am PT (calendar invite / DocuSign link to follow).

—I’ll schedule an acceptance call for 2027-09-20 at 10am PT (calendar invite / DocuSign link to follow).

—Alex
CISO, BrightBridge
Attachment stubs: Retention_Table_BrightBridge.xlsx
